data.title: Curve Dental Appoints Rick Hansen as Chief Customer Officer to Enhance Dental Software Experience
data.ai_summary: Curve Dental appointed Rick Hansen as its first Chief Customer Officer to oversee post-sales customer success, implementation, training, and support. The company has invested $200 million in customer experience and supports over 6,000 dental practices. Hansen aims to merge customer service into a cohesive journey, reducing handoffs and accelerating response times.
data.full_text:
#USA #Alpharetta #Customer Experience #Curve Dental #Rick Hansen Curve Dental Appoints Rick Hansen as Chief Customer Officer to Enhance Dental Software Experience Curve Dental Appoints Rick Hansen as Chief Customer Officer



In a significant move to enhance customer experience in the dental software sector, Curve Dental has appointed Rick Hansen as its first Chief Customer Officer. This newly established role reflects the company's commitment to providing superior service as it continues to grow and expand its customer base. With over fifteen years of experience in scaling customer success in various SaaS and healthcare domains, Hansen is set to transform how Curve serves its dental practice clients.



A New Standard for Customer Engagement



Hansen's primary responsibility will encompass the entire post-sales experience at Curve, which includes customer success management, implementation, training, and ongoing support. “When practices transition to Curve, we are not merely installing software; we take on the responsibility of ensuring their practice thrives using our system,” said Dave Cormack, CEO of Curve Dental. This philosophy underscores the importance of a seamless customer journey that integrates technology and high-touch human support.



With a $200 million investment in customer experience, Curve aims to simplify the onboarding process, streamline training and support, and ensure that practices reap the benefits of their investment in Curve software swiftly. The company believes that by investing in both people and technology, they can significantly improve the customer experience.



Connecting the Customer Journey



Hansen envisions that the customer experience should feel like a cohesive journey rather than disjointed steps. Under his leadership, Curve intends to merge various facets of customer service into a singular, fluid experience. He is focused on reducing the number of handoffs customers must navigate, thereby accelerating response times and providing a clear path to assistance throughout their relationship with Curve.



To support this initiative, Curve provides access to U.S.-based customer support teams available 24/7, ensuring that human expertise is always at hand when needed. They also leverage AI-driven resources, such as Ask CurveAI, which allows teams quick access to essential product information, further enhancing the efficiency of customer service interactions.



Embracing Technology with a Personal Touch



While utilizing technology to hasten processes is crucial, Hansen emphasizes that technology should not alienate customers from human interaction. “We want our clients to know they have a capable team ready to assist them whenever they need help. It’s about marrying technology with a personal touch,” he explained. This approach is vital for creating meaningful relationships and solidifying customer loyalty.



Rick Hansen's background includes senior positions at other well-known organizations, where he successfully enhanced their customer support operations. At Curve, he will not only lead customer engagement but also ensure that the voice of the customer is heard in product development and operational strategies.



A Vision for Growth



Rick Hansen's appointment is part of Curve Dental's broader goal to enhance the dental software landscape through innovative solutions. By supporting over 6,000 dental practices across North America, Curve is committed to facilitating their transition to cloud-based systems while ensuring they thrive in their operations.



Hansen aims to create a culture where understanding the unique challenges of dental practices is paramount. He believes that this attention to detail will make Curve a valuable partner in their clients' successes. As Hansen takes on this pivotal role, Curve Dental is set to redefine what customers can expect from a dental software provider, fostering an environment of collaboration and continuous improvement.



Through Hansen's leadership, Curve Dental is determined to elevate customer satisfaction by integrating advanced technology with an exceptional human touch, ensuring dental practices can focus on what they do best—providing excellent care to their patients.

data.full_text:
Appointment accelerates Curve's investment in customer onboarding and implementation, training, support and long-term success—combining high-touch human expertise with modern technology to make every stage of the customer journey faster, easier and more connected ALPHARETTA, Ga., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Curve Dental®, the leader in AI-powered, cloud-native, all-in-one dental practice management software, today announced the appointment of Rick Hansen as Chief Customer Officer, a newly created executive role reflecting Curve's fast-paced growth and expanding customer base. Hansen is charged with transforming the experience customers receive from implementation and go-live through ongoing support, adoption and growth. Continue Reading

Rick Hansen, Chief Customer Officer at Curve Dental, will lead Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Training and Account Management as the company expands its investment in a more connected, high-touch customer experience. Hansen will lead Curve's post-sales organization, including Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Training and Account Management. His mandate is to connect those functions around one customer journey, modernize how Curve serves practices at scale and raise the standard for what dental teams should expect from their software partner. The role also supports Curve's continued expansion with multi-location groups and DSOs, where implementation, standardization, training and ongoing support become increasingly complex as organizations scale. The appointment extends the same long-term investment philosophy behind Curve's recently announced $200 million R&D commitment into the customer experience around the platform. As Curve continues to grow, the company is investing in both the people and technology that help practices transition successfully, reach value faster and get the right help when they need it. "When a practice moves to Curve, we're not just installing software. We're being trusted with the system that keeps their business running," said Dave Cormack, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Curve Dental. "That means we are with our customers every step of the way: in the lead-up to going live, through the conversion and training, and long after the switch is made. We want our customers to know that Curve is truly part of their team—not simply a vendor they call when something breaks." "At the same time, we're continuing our investment in AI and automation to make the simple things faster, because no one should have to wait for an answer that should take seconds," added Cormack. "But technology should never become a wall between us and the customer. When a practice needs a person, they have always been able to reach a knowledgeable Curve team member who can listen, use judgment and help them move forward. Rick's mandate is to raise the standard on both sides of that equation: make us faster through technology and more valuable through our people." From Implementation to Long-Term Success For dental practices, changing practice management systems is not a simple software purchase. It can touch years of data, workflows across the front office and clinical team, training, billing, reporting and the daily rhythm of the practice. Curve's customer model is designed around supporting that change before, during and after go-live—not handing a practice a login and wishing them luck. Under Hansen's leadership, Curve will continue strengthening implementation and onboarding while bringing Training, Support, Customer Success and Account Management into a more connected experience. Working closely with Kristen Smith, Vice President of Customer Success and a 17-year Curve veteran, Hansen will build on the deep customer relationships and institutional knowledge already in place as the organization scales. The goal is to reduce handoffs, accelerate time-to-value and give customers a clearer path to help throughout the life of the relationship. Curve customers have access to U.S.-based, Curve-trained support 24/7 when a situation calls for human expertise. At the same time, self-service and AI-powered resources such as Ask CurveAI complement live support by giving teams immediate access to routine product guidance and answers, and speed up resolution time when human-led support is needed. By using technology to remove unnecessary waiting and repetitive work, Curve creates more capacity for its Customer Success team to focus on the higher-value moments where context, judgment and partnership matter most. "Customer experience shouldn't feel like a series of handoffs," said Hansen. "It should feel like one team from the first implementation conversation through every stage of the customer relationship. My focus is connecting those moments, making it easier for practices to get value from Curve and making sure we are there with the right level of help before customers have to fight to find it." "Technology gives us the ability to be faster, more proactive and more consistent. Just as important, it gives our people more time to do the work only people can do well—understand the customer, solve complex problems and build trusted relationships," added Hansen. "That combination is where I believe the customer experience is going, and it's what we intend to build at Curve." Building a Customer Organization for Growth Hansen brings more than 15 years of experience building and scaling post-sales organizations across SaaS, dental, healthcare and other technology markets. His background includes leading Customer Success, Training, Implementation and Support teams and deploying technology, AI-enabled tools and automation to improve customer experience and operational efficiency. Prior to joining Curve, Hansen held senior customer leadership roles at Weave, where he led Customer Success Management, Training, Implementation and Customer Support and helped guide the company through its 2021 IPO. Earlier, he spent more than seven years at Instructure, ultimately overseeing a global organization spanning Customer Success, Implementation, Training and Support while helping the company expand internationally across APAC, EMEA and Latin America. At Curve, Hansen will also serve as a senior voice for the customer across the business, bringing customer feedback and experience data into product and operational decisions as the company continues to expand its platform. Curve supports more than 6,000 dental practice locations across North America, including clinics operating within shared multi-location databases. The company's continued investment in product innovation and customer experience is designed to help practices not only move to the cloud, but operate with greater confidence once they are there. About Curve Dental Curve Dental provides an AI-powered, cloud-native operating platform designed to help dental practices manage and grow their businesses while giving teams more time to focus on patient care. Curve brings together practice management, clinical workflows, revenue cycle capabilities, payments, patient engagement and an expanding ecosystem of connected solutions, with AI and automation increasingly embedded across workflows to reduce administrative burden and make practices easier to run. Curve Dental serves dental professionals and practices across the United States and Canada and is privately held, with operations in Provo, Utah; Alpharetta, Georgia; Calgary, Alberta; and Aberdeen, Scotland. Curve Dental is proud to be named a 2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces award winner. Visit www.curvedental.com or call 1-888-910-HERO for more information. SOURCE Curve Dental

AI can automate tasks such as image analysis and patient chart updates which save dentists and staff time and reduce administrative overhead. Integrated seamlessly with Curve, Curve Memberships helps practices identify enrollment opportunities, automate patient outreach and keep payments connected to billing and collections ALPHARETTA, Ga., Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Curve Dental®, the leader in AI-powered, cloud-native, all-in-one dental practice management software, today announced Curve Memberships, designed to help practices identify patients who could benefit from an in-house dental membership plan, simplify enrollment and build more predictable recurring revenue. Continue Reading

Curve Memberships works seamlessly with Curve Dental practice management software to help practices manage enrollment, membership payments and member activity alongside the workflows they already use every day. Curve Memberships works seamlessly with the patient information dental teams already manage in Curve. Practices can engage uninsured patients and those interested in services outside their insurance coverage—such as whitening and other elective care not covered by their plan—while creating a simpler path to membership enrollment. Once patients enroll, membership payments automatically post to the patient account in Curve, keeping membership billing, collections and patient records connected to the system the practice already uses every day. The result is stronger patient loyalty and a more streamlined membership experience for the practice. "Dental membership plans work—until they become one more thing the front desk has to remember, " said Luke Anderson, Chief Product Officer at Curve Dental. "Curve Memberships connects with the software the team already uses all day, so identifying patients, driving enrollment and managing membership payments becomes part of the workflow—not more tasks to manage. That means practices can grow revenue without adding more work to the team's day." Turning the Schedule Into an Enrollment Engine More than 1 in 5 working-age U.S. adults have no dental benefits, according to the American Dental Association Health Policy Institute, underscoring the need for more flexible ways for patients to access and pay for dental care. In-house dental membership plans can help meet that need, but they often depend on staff recognizing an opportunity, explaining the program during a busy patient interaction and remembering to follow up afterward. Curve Memberships streamlines that process by automatically delivering personalized invitations, helping practices grow enrollment without maintaining separate lists, spreadsheets or manual outreach campaigns. For patients, these plans provide a straightforward, subscription-style way to understand the cost and value of their care. For practices, they can strengthen loyalty and create a more direct, predictable financial relationship with patients. Memberships that Support a Healthier Practice A healthy, growing practice doesn't have to depend on insurance reimbursement alone. Membership plans can help create more predictable recurring revenue while reducing some of the administrative burden that comes with insurance-based care. They can also support case acceptance by giving patients clearer, more approachable costs for services they may otherwise delay or decline—particularly care that falls outside insurance coverage. Dental membership plans create a more direct relationship between the practice and patient, helping practices strengthen loyalty while giving patients a clearer path to care they value. Practices can also use the reports they already rely on in Curve to see production and collections trends across their membership patients and better understand the impact of their program. "Membership-driven care gives practices more control over the economics of care while giving patients a clearer way to say yes to treatment," said Anderson. "Curve Memberships helps make that easier to manage—from identifying opportunities and enrollment through payments and performance." Built for the Way Practices Work Curve Memberships connects membership information with the patient record and everyday workflows dental teams already manage in Curve, giving teams greater visibility into member status and relevant care opportunities without adding another disconnected process. Practices also receive dedicated support for setup and launch, along with a marketing toolkit designed to help introduce, promote and build participation in their membership program. With Curve Memberships, practices can: Identify patients who may benefit from a membership plan

Automatically deliver personalized invitations

See membership information within existing patient workflows

Auto-post payments to the patient account in Curve

Launch and promote plans with dedicated support and marketing resources

Reduce manual tracking, spreadsheets and disconnected processes

data.ai_summary: Curve Dental promoted Luke Anderson to Chief Product Officer as it accelerates its product roadmap and deploys a $200 million research and development commitment. The company, approaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue, serves over 6,000 dental practice locations. Anderson will lead global product strategy across AI, automation, and connected workflows.
data.author: Paul Bluemner
data.full_text:
Atlanta, Global General Business, Healthcare, People Curve Dental Promotes Luke Anderson to Chief Product Officer Amid $200M R&D Push

Dental practices increasingly depend on software to manage clinical care, payments, patient engagement and administrative work, but disconnected systems can leave staff moving between applications and duplicating tasks. Curve Dental is betting that a more integrated cloud platform, supported by AI and automation, can reduce that operational burden. The Alpharetta, Georgia-based dental software company has promoted Luke Anderson to Chief Product Officer as it accelerates its product roadmap and deploys a recently announced $200 million research and development commitment. Curve is also approaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue and serves more than 6,000 dental practice locations across North America. Anderson joined Curve in 2025 as Senior Vice President of Product, overseeing product and user experience. As CPO, he will lead the company’s global product strategy and roadmap across AI, automation, connected workflows and continued development of its end-to-end cloud platform. “The pressures on dental teams have changed dramatically, but many of the solutions in this industry haven’t kept pace,” Curve Chairman and CEO Dave Cormack said. Cormack said Anderson will be responsible for translating the company’s investment in product development into technology intended to simplify practice operations. Curve’s strategy centers on creating a cloud platform that can support practices as they grow rather than requiring them to assemble separate products for different functions. The promotion comes during a period of significant expansion for Curve. The company said its growth toward $100 million in annual recurring revenue has been driven almost entirely organically. Its additional $200 million R&D commitment is intended to support further development of its software platform and new capabilities. Curve combines practice management, clinical workflows, revenue cycle functions, payments, patient engagement and AI within a single cloud-based environment. The company’s product strategy is aimed at reducing the technology fragmentation that can occur when dental practices rely on separate systems for clinical, financial, administrative and patient-facing work. For dental teams, the operational value of that approach depends less on adding individual AI features than on integrating automation into workflows employees already use. Curve is focusing on areas where software can eliminate repetitive tasks, connect information across functions and reduce the amount of manual coordination required to operate a practice. “The opportunity here is bigger than shipping more features,” Anderson said. “Our job is to listen to dental teams, find where technology slows them down instead of helping, and fix that — simply, and in ways that actually work together.” Anderson brings more than two decades of experience across product strategy, artificial intelligence and machine learning, SaaS, private equity and management consulting. Before joining Curve, he led AI and machine learning initiatives at Chick-fil-A. He also served as Head of Product at OfficeSpace Software, where he led product strategy during a period in which the company’s annual recurring revenue nearly tripled. Earlier in his career, Anderson worked at Resurgens Technology Partners and Bain & Company. He began his career as an officer in the U.S. Marine Corps, serving in leadership as well as product and program management roles. He graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy and earned an MBA from the University of Virginia’s Darden School of Business. Curve’s expansion has also attracted industry recognition. Healthcare business advisory firm HealthStream Ventures identified Curve as the cloud-native leader in dental software in 2026. The company was also named a 2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces award winner. Curve is privately held and serves dental professionals across the United States and Canada. In addition to Alpharetta, it has operations in Provo, Utah; Calgary, Alberta; and Aberdeen, Scotland. The company plans to announce a series of product launches and additional platform capabilities in the coming weeks. Anderson will oversee that next stage of development as Curve puts its expanded R&D budget toward building more connected dental workflows and embedding AI and automation into day-to-day practice operations.

#United States #Alpharetta #Dental Software #Curve Dental #Curve Hero Curve Dental Sets Ambitious $200 Million R&D Investment to Revolutionize Dental Software Market Introduction

Curve Dental, a leader in AI-driven dental software, has announced a stunning investment of $200 million aimed at enhancing its integrated end-to-end cloud platform known as Curve Hero. This substantial funding underscores the company’s commitment to revolutionizing the dental software market, particularly at a time when it is nearing $100 million in annual recurring revenue.



Investment Overview

Since its founding, Curve Dental has demonstrated remarkable growth, particularly since 2018, when it began seeing rapid customer adoption. This growth has supported a sustained commitment to reinvest in research and development, dedicating tens of millions of dollars annually towards both product development and enhanced customer service. As it currently holds about 20% of the cloud dental practice market, the company has solidified its reputation by offering best-in-class, natively integrated functionalities that cater specifically to single-location, small-group, and dental service organization (DSO) practices.



Leadership Insights

CEO and Chairman Dave Cormack, a seasoned veteran with over 40 years in high-growth software companies, reflected on the journey Curve Dental has undertaken, pointing out that the existing market primarily relies on outdated client-server solutions that have not kept pace with technological advancements.



"Nine years ago, we realized that there was a tremendous opportunity to not just compete but to lead in the dental software space. Curve provided an excellent foundation for crafting a fully integrated, end-to-end cloud platform designed specifically for the needs of modern dental practices," Cormack said.



Having invested over $100 million in R&D within the last eight years, Curve Dental has transitioned to a fully native platform that supports a variety of functions such as patient engagement, intelligent phone integration, advanced eligibility checks, and more—all under a single sign-on. This comprehensive approach ensures that dental practices can optimize their operations without the need for managing multiple software solutions from different vendors.



Market Dynamics

As the company prepares for significant changes in the dental software landscape, Cormack highlighted the impending transformation as practices shift away from legacy systems to integrated cloud platforms. He predicts that more than 40% of practice management software vendors may not survive the next 36 to 48 months due to an oversaturation in the market and inadequate innovation from competitors who struggle to keep pace in R&D and customer service.



"A dental software death spiral is upon us, as many vendors have burnt through cash to gain market share without investing in the actual advancements needed to sustain their products," he explained.



Strategic Focus

Going forward, Curve Dental is laser-focused on delivering unparalleled service and value to its customers. Cormack emphasized that the company’s success hinges on the success of its clients, stating, "We measure our success by our customers' achievements and continuously strive to provide exceptional support and advancements in our offerings. Our commitment to enhancing the Curve Hero platform will ensure practices always have the most effective tools and capabilities at their disposal."



As Curve continues to scale rapidly in both client acquisition and technological advancements, it's setting a robust precedent for what modern dental practices can achieve through strategic investment and a focus on integrated solutions. With a workforce that embodies passion for both innovation and customer satisfaction, Curve Dental is poised to lead the industry into a new era of efficiency and effectiveness.



About Curve Dental

As a privately held entity, Curve Dental operates not only across North America but is also recognized in various international markets for its pioneering solutions. With operations in Provo, Utah; Alpharetta, Georgia; Calgary, Alberta; and Aberdeen, Scotland, Curve Dental remains steadfast in its mission to empower dental professionals with the most advanced tools in the field.



For additional insights on Curve Dental and its transformations in dental practice management, visit their website or contact them for further information.

data.full_text: As Curve Approaches $100 Million in Annual Recurring Revenue, Chairman and CEO Dave Cormack Predicts Major Shift in Dental Software Market ALPHARETTA, Ga., Aug. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Curve Dental®, the leader in modern AI-driven all-in-one dental software with an integrated end-to-end cloud platform, today announced a further $200 million investment in its Curve Hero product and comprehensive ecosystem of native best-in-class capabilities. Record-breaking year-over-year growth since 2018, driven by rapid customer adoption, has enabled Curve to reinvest tens of millions of dollars each year in product development and customer services. The company is rapidly approaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue, almost entirely generated through organic growth. With around 20% of the cloud dental practice market, Curve is fulfilling its promise to deliver best-in-class native functionality for single-location, small-group, and DSO practices—without requiring customers to contract with and manage multiple software vendors. Recognizing market demand for an open platform, Curve’s API capability supports vendor integrations that meet rigorous standards for quality, security, reliability, interoperability and customer experience. Dave Cormack, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Curve Dental and a 40-year veteran of high-growth software companies, reflected on the company’s journey: “Nine years ago, today’s leadership team at Curve, having previously grown Brightree from a startup to the most successful cloud software platform in the homecare market, fell in love with the opportunity to deliver the most compelling solution for the dental industry when we saw that close to 100% of the market was relying on 20- to 30-year-old client-server solutions. No other opportunity in healthcare came close. “We acquired Curve Dental because it provided an excellent foundation for us to build a fully integrated, end-to-end cloud platform. In my experience, multi-practice software cannot be scaled down for single locations or small-group practices. It must be built natively from the ground up—and that is exactly what we did. “After $100 million of R&D investment in the last eight years, Curve has continually modernized into a fully native, single sign-on platform for solo practices to small multi-location groups and DSOs, including patient engagement, intelligent phone integration, advanced eligibility, credit card payments, auto payment posting, RCM, membership plans, orthodontics workflow, business intelligence and more. Curve is giving the dental industry a new way to practice and a better way to grow.” Investing for the Long Term Cormack said Curve’s financial position gives practices confidence that the company will continue investing for the long term: “As a $100 million annual recurring revenue business, we are profitable and growing while reinvesting tens of millions of dollars each year in product development and customer services. As such, the dental market can be confident that we are here for the long term. “My strong advice to any dental practice considering a move to a cloud system is to make sure that the software vendor is profitable, so it can continue to reinvest, and compare what they plan to spend on research and development against Curve’s $200 million commitment.” Reflecting on Curve’s extensive R&D commitment and what he believes will be a major consolidation of the dental software market, Cormack said: “Our leadership has lived this journey many times and, as they say, we’ve seen this movie before, bought the T-shirt, and we always deliver for our customers. “With 85% of the roughly 160,000 dental practices in North America still on a legacy client-server system, Curve will focus all its efforts on delivering the most compelling native end-to-end cloud platform in the market—one that meets the needs of practices of all sizes and stages of growth, so that they’ll never outgrow Curve. “We will achieve that by continuing to hire and retain great people who have a passion and desire to delight our customers. It’s the only way.” A Market at an Inflection Point Cormack believes the shift from legacy client-server systems to integrated cloud platforms will also drive significant consolidation across the dental software market over the next several years. “A dental software death spiral is upon us. As the market rapidly shifts from legacy systems to the cloud, the vendor market across the ecosystem is oversaturated—from core practice-management platforms to add-on solutions for patient engagement, analytics, imaging and more. “But moving to the cloud is only part of the equation. Practices should look beyond the cloud label to understand how a platform has actually been built and how well its products work together. While Curve has been 100% natively-built, many competitors have acquired a mismatched collection of products that leaves practices with fragmented data, multiple user interfaces, inconsistent workflows and integration complexity. These platforms do anything but operate as one unified system. “I predict that over 40 percent of practice management software vendors, with an alarming number burning through cash to buy market share at the expense of R&D and customer services, will not exist in 36 to 48 months. The same pressure will affect point solutions that create more complexity than differentiated customer value, as AI-driven cloud platforms increasingly deliver those capabilities natively in a fully integrated manner and at a lower total cost of ownership than practices currently employ through licensing software from five or six different vendors. Cormack concluded by returning to Curve’s commitment to its customers: “Our customers’ success is how we measure our own success. We work to earn their business every single day by listening, responding promptly and continually keeping the Curve Hero platform ahead of our competition. “If you haven’t seen Curve in action recently—or at all—I encourage you to talk with us about the challenges you face and see how we can better serve you.” About Curve Dental Curve Dental provides an intelligent, cloud-based operating platform designed to help dental practices manage and grow their businesses while giving teams more time to focus on patient care. Curve brings together practice management, clinical workflows, revenue cycle capabilities, payments, patient engagement, artificial intelligence, and an expanding ecosystem of connected solutions in one platform built for modern dentistry. Curve Dental serves dental professionals and practices across the United States and Canada and is privately held, with operations in Provo, Utah; Alpharetta, Georgia; Calgary, Alberta; and Aberdeen, Scotland. Curve Dental is proud to be named a 2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces award winner. Visit www.curvedental.com or call 1-888-910-HERO for more information. That represents an absolute dollar opportunity of $6.9Bn. Dental offices now use AI software for more than reviewing images, weaving it into daily work such as booking appointments, recording visits, processing insurance claims, and communicating with patients, while dentists still make all final clinical decisions. What Is Changing in How Practices Specify AI Software? Dental offices are using software to send reminders, confirm visits, fill open slots, and follow up with patients who miss appointments, protecting daily income against empty chair time. Billing staff use the same tools to check insurance coverage, prepare claims, and follow up on rejections, and dentists are more likely to adopt clinical AI when staff can review its work, track changes, and correct mistakes. Which Deployments and Functions Lead the Market? Cloud-based deployment leads at about 38.3% share, supported by browser access, automatic updates, and shared use across several locations, ahead of on-premise and hybrid models. Appointment scheduling and automation tops AI-function demand at roughly 25%, since a missed visit leaves a chair empty and cuts daily income, and practice management leads application demand at close to 30% by bringing appointments, records, billing, and daily reports into one system. Solo dental practices place about 30% of end-user demand. Which Countries Present the Strongest Growth? Germany leads at a 23.1% CAGR through 2036 on better appointment control and chair-utilisation planning, with Brazil close behind at 21.4% on billing automation and multi-site workflows. The United States follows at 19.7% on dental-group growth and insurance processing, ahead of South Korea (18.0%), the United Kingdom (16.2%), and Japan (14.5%). What Could Slow Adoption? Clinical-control and human-override requirements are the main brake, since practices may avoid AI tools when dentists cannot see how a result was created or changed, and each system needs simple review and rejection steps. Unreliable or poorly governed generative AI outputs add a second constraint, as inaccurate notes or suggestions increase the chance that wrong information enters a patient record or message. How Are Suppliers Responding? Henry Schein One and Planet DDS lead through wide dental practice software ranges, with Henry Schein One announcing AWS-backed generative AI work and Planet DDS pairing cloud practice software with Pearl39s AI image review. Carestream Dental and Curve Dental provide cloud software and imaging links, while Denti.AI, VideaHealth, Pearl, and Overjet focus more narrowly on clinical and imaging AI. Competition centres on how well tasks work together and whether automation keeps the dentist in control. What Should Practices and DSOs Monitor Through 2036? Separate tasks the software handles on its own from those requiring staff review, and confirm a simple correction process exists for fixing wrong results. Test any new setup at a few locations before applying it across a larger group, and confirm data security, data ownership, service support, and export options in customer agreements before committing to one software company. Embedded directly into the Curve platform, Curve Care+ introduces three native AI-powered solutions—Notes+, Charting+, and Perio+—giving dental teams ambient intelligence that lives in their existing clinical workflows, without bolted-on extensions, separate logins, or disconnected third-party tools. “Dental teams are under constant pressure to do more with less time,” said Suzanne Henderson, Chief Technology Officer at Curve Dental. “Curve Care+ was built to further simplify the tools providers already use every day, helping teams work more efficiently while preserving the human connection at the center of patient care.” A New Approach to Clinical Documentation Curve Care+ is designed around a simple goal: ensuring documentation happens while care is happening—not during lunch breaks, between appointments, or after hours. Offered as part of the broader Curve+ AI Suite, the Curve Care+ clinical AI solution includes the following: Notes+ ambiently captures clinical conversations and drafts provider-ready notes in either SOAP format or the practice’s own templates.

Creating More Capacity Across the Clinical Day As staffing challenges continue to affect practices, Curve Care+ serves as a workforce multiplier, helping providers and hygienists complete documentation more efficiently, reduce administrative burden, and create additional clinical capacity without increasing headcount. Minimize after-hours charting and administrative work

Complete restorative and periodontal charting through voice-driven workflows

These efficiencies help practices do more with existing staff while maintaining a high standard of care. Building the Future of Dental Practice Management The launch of Curve Care+ marks another step in Curve Dental’s strategy to bring purpose-built intelligence into clinical, financial, and patient engagement workflows. “We are focused on practical AI that solves real operational challenges across the practice, from clinical documentation to revenue cycle and patient engagement, without forcing teams into disconnected systems,” added Henderson. But with a crowded market — and every vendor website saying the same things: all-in-one, intuitive, cloud-native, scalable. It can get a little overwhelming. So we did the digging for you. We looked at four of the most talked-about cloud-based practice management systems right now — CareStack, Curve Dental, Denticon, and Dentrix Ascend — and put together an honest, non-biased breakdown: what each system does, what real users are saying in verified reviews, and who each one is genuinely the best fit for. And, as a dental IT provider who has experience troubleshooting and working with cloud PMS... we’ve included some critical considerations as you explore moving your dental practice to a cloud practice management system. There's no ranked list (their in alphabetical order) or winner here. The right PMS for a private general dental practice in Phoenix looks very different from the right solution for a 10-location dental organization on the East Coast.

Looking for a broader dental practice management software comparison that includes server-based or hybrid systems like Dentrix, Eaglesoft, and Open Dental? We covered those - including a full list of dental software programs across deployment types - in our previous article: Top Practice Management Software for Dental Practices. This article focuses specifically on cloud-first solutions for practices ready to leave the server behind. What to Look for in a Cloud-Based Dental PMS Before we get into the individual systems, here are the factors worth weighing as you compare: True cloud vs. cloud-hosted: Is it built for the cloud from the ground up, or is it a legacy system running through a remote desktop?

Ease of use and training time: A powerful system no one knows how to use is a liability, not an asset.

Integrations: Does it work with your imaging software, payment processor, and patient communication tools... or will you be managing a patchwork of add-ons?

Reporting and analytics: Can you get the numbers you need without needing a degree in data science to run a report?

Support quality: What does onboarding look like? What happens when something goes wrong at 3PM on a Wednesday?

Scalability: Will this system grow with you, or will you outgrow it in two years?

Total cost of ownership: Monthly fees are just the beginning. Factor in onboarding, training, add-ons, and data export.

Data portability: If you ever need to switch, can you get your patient records out without a fight? Whether you're new to evaluating dental software programs or you're coming off a legacy system and ready to modernize, these criteria apply regardless of which platform you're considering. CareStack Website: carestack.com

G2 Rating: 4.7/5 (176 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.8/5 (189 reviews) Overview CareStack is an all-in-one, cloud-based dental practice management platform built to serve everything from single-office practices to large, enterprise-level DSOs. The software covers scheduling, clinical charting, treatment planning, billing, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient communications, and analytics — all without the need for third-party add-ons. More than 2,500 dental practices across the U.S. use CareStack. It holds the #1 ranking on G2 for dental practice management software, is certified in HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001:2022, and has been the subject of a Forrester Total Economic Impact™ study that suggests the platform can pay for itself within six months for multi-location practices. CareStack has also been actively expanding its AI capabilities — including AI-driven telephony (VoiceStack™) and AI-powered imaging analysis (Aeka™). What CareStack Users Say "I have been working with CareStack for over 4 years, and the team is amazing — very professional and knowledgeable. The PMS offers comprehensive systems that enable practices to grow both internally and externally, making it an excellent solution for DSOs." — G2 Verified Review "There is a bit of a learning curve at first because the system has so many features. Once you get used to it, though, it becomes much easier to navigate." — G2 Verified Review Pros Truly all-in-one: scheduling, charting, billing, patient communications, RCM, and analytics in a single platform with no required add-ons

Strong multi-location capabilities: centralized reporting and cross-practice operations from one dashboard

Excellent customer support and onboarding: consistently cited as a differentiator in user reviews

Active product development: users report seeing their feature requests implemented

AI-powered growth tools available as part of the ecosystem (VoiceStack™, Aeka™) Cons Steeper learning curve: the depth of features requires meaningful investment in training, especially for teams new to cloud software

Implementation timeline: onboarding can take approximately two months, and some features have been flagged as still "in development" at go-live

Billing workflows can feel multi-step: some users note that billing processes require more clicks than comparable systems

Pricing requires a custom quote: not publicly listed, which makes early budgeting harder

Dependent on internet connectivity: like all cloud systems, a downed connection means disrupted workflow until it's restored Best Suited For CareStack is an excellent fit for growth-oriented practices — whether that's a single office planning to expand, a multi-location group looking to standardize operations, or a DSO that needs enterprise-level visibility and scalability. If your goal is to reduce your vendor count and gain real-time cross-location reporting, CareStack deserves a close look. That said, if your team is small and you need to be up and running quickly without a significant learning curve, the feature depth may feel like more than you need right now. Curve Dental Website: curvedental.com

G2 Rating: 4.6/5 (165 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.4/5 (285 reviews) Overview Curve Dental is one of the original cloud-native dental practice management platforms — built for the cloud from day one, not adapted to it after the fact. This means the system was designed around the realities of browser-based access, mobile flexibility, and continuous delivery of updates — not retrofitted from a legacy product. Trusted by over 80,000 dental professionals across practices of all sizes, Curve offers a comprehensive suite: scheduling, charting, billing, patient intake, treatment planning, automated insurance verification, membership plans, and dashboard reporting — all in one platform. The company also claims customers report up to 20% higher collections, 25% more new patients, and 30% better case acceptance after adopting the system. Curve has also introduced a Curve Mobile experience and continues to integrate AI partners like Pearl and Bola AI for imaging and treatment acceptance improvements. What Curve Dental Users Say “I love using Curve Hero—it makes managing our dental office so much smoother and more organized. The cloud-based system is fast, intuitive, and keeps everything from scheduling to billing perfectly streamlined.” — Software Advice Verified Review “Main benefit I’ve found with Curve is that it is pretty intuitive, which makes it easy to train people who have not used the program. However, we have had issues with rotating outages on Curve for the past year...” — Curve User | Reddit (r/Dentistry - Cloud Based PMS guidance) Pros Clean, intuitive interface: consistently rated easy to learn, with minimal onboarding time

Strong patient engagement tools: automated reminders, two-way texting, SmartFill for wait-list management

Competitive pricing: one of the more accessible entry points among cloud platforms

Highly rated customer support: a consistent highlight in user reviews

Curve Mobile: browser-based mobile access for on-the-go schedule and patient management Cons Reporting depth: some users report that reporting feels less sophisticated compared to enterprise systems, particularly for multi-location analytics

Limited specialty customization: may not meet the complex charting needs of orthodontists, periodontists, or oral surgeons without add-ons

Cloud-only which means full internet dependency

Insurance estimate accuracy: some users note occasional inaccuracies in insurance estimates

Less customizable than open-source or enterprise-level alternatives Best Suited For Curve Dental is an excellent choice for independent practices, dental startups, and small-to-mid-sized multi-location groups that want a modern, polished, and easy-to-use system without the complexity of enterprise software. If minimizing training time, reducing IT costs, and getting staff up and running quickly are priorities, Curve consistently delivers. It's also worth noting for practices coming off server-based systems like Eaglesoft or legacy Dentrix — Curve's user experience tends to feel like a natural leap forward without the steep learning curve of more feature-heavy platforms. Denticon by Planet DDS Website: planetdds.com/denticon

G2 Rating: 4.7/5 (74 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.5/5 (112 reviews) Overview Denticon, developed by Planet DDS, is a cloud-based practice management system built specifically for multi-location dental groups and DSOs. Unlike platforms that started as single-practice solutions and scaled up, Denticon was designed from the beginning to handle the operational complexity of enterprise dental organizations — centralized scheduling, cross-location reporting, multi-specialty workflows, and consolidated RCM at scale. Used by more than 13,000 dental practices, including notable DSO brands like Park Dental, Smile Brands, D4C, and Dental Care Alliance, Denticon positions itself as the operational backbone for high-growth dental businesses. The platform includes a full suite of clinical, front office, and reporting tools, as well as newer additions like AI Voice Perio charting, AI Voice Restorative charting, and AI Assist for proactive patient treatment insights. Planet DDS also offers Apteryx XVWeb — a cloud-based dental imaging solution that integrates directly with Denticon, providing a companion to the practice management platform. What Denticon Users Say "In the last 10 years of using Planet DDS, we have grown from 2 to 11 locations. The ease of use of the product is unmatched. The conversion process is seamless, and the support team is phenomenal." — G2 Verified Review Pros Purpose-built for multi-location and DSO operations: centralized visibility, reporting, and management across all locations from a single platform

Comprehensive RCM tools: batch claims, automated eligibility verification (AutoEligibility), 835 auto-posting, and revenue dashboards

Strong implementation and data conversion support: Planet DDS has experience converting data from nearly every PMS

Morning Huddle dashboard: a standout feature that helps teams start the day aligned on production goals and schedule priorities

Proven track record with enterprise clients: 20+ years in market, with large DSO references Cons Interface can feel dated: multiple users note the UI could benefit from a visual refresh, though Planet DDS acknowledges ongoing work here

Analytics learning curve: while reporting is powerful, some users find the analytics setup complex to configure correctly

Not ideal for solo or small single-location practices: the feature depth and complexity is calibrated for larger organizations Best Suited For Denticon is the right platform for multi-location dental groups, growing DSOs, and enterprise dental organizations that need a cloud-based system capable of handling real operational scale. If you're managing multiple providers and locations, need centralized RCM, and are evaluating against other DSO-grade platforms, Denticon belongs on your shortlist. For smaller, independent single-location practices, the complexity and pricing model may be more than what you need. Lighter, more accessible platforms like Curve Dental or CareStack may serve you better. Dentrix Ascend Website: dentrixascend.com

G2 Rating: 4.3/5 (18 reviews)

Software Advice Rating: 4.1/5 (234 reviews) Overview Dentrix Ascend is the cloud-based evolution of Dentrix — one of the most established names in dental practice management software. Built by Henry Schein One, Ascend takes the brand recognition and deep dental industry roots of legacy Dentrix and moves them into a fully cloud-native environment. The platform covers scheduling, billing, clinical charting, imaging, AI-powered diagnostics, patient communications, and real-time analytics. Ascend has also recently added features like Reserve with Google integration (allowing new patients to book directly through search results), AI-powered call summaries, Voice Notes for hands-free charting documentation, and automated insurance eligibility verification. Over 80,000 clinicians, office managers, and staff use Dentrix Ascend today, with 83% of insurance claims processed annually through the platform. Ascend is not a direct cloud port of legacy Dentrix. It's a rebuilt product with its own workflows — so even longtime Dentrix users may face a learning adjustment. What Dentrix Ascend Users Say “I love how easy Dentrix Ascend is to navigate. It allows me to efficiently move from the patient side to the prescription side and also manages the clinic side seamlessly." — G2 Verified Review “The layout isn't intuitive, and getting meaningful, relevant data often feels like a complex puzzle — honestly, you'd need a PhD in Power Reporting just to make it useful." — Software Advice Verified Review Pros True cloud platform: no servers, no VPNs, accessible from any device with internet

Strong brand trust: built by Henry Schein One, a well-established player in dental technology

AI-powered tools: built-in AI imaging analysis, Voice Notes, and call summaries

Reserve with Google: enables online booking directly from Google search results

Active feature development — Henry Schein One listens to user feedback and regularly releases updates Cons Reporting complexity: multiple users cite the "Power Reporting" feature as unintuitive and difficult to use effectively

Limited third-party integrations at speed: integrations with tools like GoTo or Weave can take longer than expected

Pricing opacity: pricing is not publicly listed; custom quotes required

No dedicated mobile app: browser-based mobile access works, but there's no native iOS or Android app

Data migration challenges: some users report that migrating existing patient data into Ascend was time-consuming Best Suited For Dentrix Ascend is a strong option for practices that already know and trust the Dentrix brand but are ready to move away from on-premise infrastructure. It's particularly well-suited for practices of all sizes that want a clean cloud experience with built-in AI clinical tools, solid security credentials, and the backing of a major industry vendor. One G2 reviewer noted that Ascend supported 280% organizational growth over four years — so for practices in an active growth phase, it's worth a serious look. But, if extensive custom reporting or deep third-party integrations are critical to your workflow, it's worth demoing those specific features carefully before committing. Dental Practice Management Software Comparison: Cloud-Based Systems at a Glance CareStack Curve Dental Denticon Dentrix Ascend G2 Rating 4.7/5 (176) 4.6/5 (165) 4.7/5 (74) 4.3/5 (18) Software Advice Rating 4.8/5 (189) 4.4/5 (285) 4.5/5 (112) 4.1/5 (234) Best Suited For Growth-focused practices & DSOs Startups, independent & small-mid groups Multi-location groups & DSOs Practices familiar with Dentrix; all sizes AI Features VoiceStack™, Aeka™ Pearl & Bola AI partners AI Voice Perio/Restorative, AI Assist AI imaging, Voice Notes Multi-Location Support Strong Moderate Built for it Strong Learning Curve Moderate-High Low-Moderate Moderate-High Moderate Support Reputation Highly rated Highly rated Mixed Generally positive 5 Questions to Ask Before You Choose a Cloud PMS for Your Dental Practice Choosing the best dental practice management software for your practice isn't just about feature checkllists - it's about finding the right fit for how your team works. Before you schedule a demo, get clear on your own answers to these questions: What does "all-in-one" mean to your practice specifically?

Every vendor uses this phrase. What does your practiceactually need in one system — and what are you happy to manage with a best-in-class third-party tool? What does your growth plan look like in the next 3–5 years?

Ifyou're planning to add locations, bring on associate dentists, or eventually pursue a dental organization structure, your PMS needs to be able to grow with you before you outgrow it. What are your staff'stechnical comfort levels?

A feature-rich system that your team struggles to use is an expensive liability. Honest conversations about training time and learning curves matter more than demos. What reporting do you need,and how often?

If you review production, collections, and AR weekly, make sure the system can generate those reports in a way your team can realistically use. Ask to see the actual reporting interface... not just a screenshot. What happens to your data if you ever need to switch?

It's not a fun question, butit's a necessary one. Ask each vendor directly: Can I export my patient records, images, and notes? Is there a fee? How long does it take? Their answer will tell you a lot. Before You Make the Switch - Your IT Setup Matters Here's something that doesn't always come up in PMS conversations, but absolutely should: cloud-based software is only as strong as the infrastructure it runs on. And the stakes are real. A thread on r/Dentistry captured it plainly — when an AWS outage took down several cloud-based practice management systems, dental practices that had gone cloud-only were left with two choices: reschedule appointments or revert to paper charting and manually upload everything later. (4) This isn’t a knock on cloud software. It's a reminder that the move to cloud doesn't eliminate infrastructure risk — it shifts it. And if your network, connectivity, and contingency plan aren't solid, you'll feel every gap. We've seen this play out firsthand.

A dental practice came to us mid-evaluation for cloud-based PMS — excited to ditch their aging server, simplify operations, and finally access their data from anywhere. But they wanted to ensure their network could handle the shift. Their existing internet connection was adequate for a server-based workflow, but it wasn’t adequate for a fully cloud-dependent system at peak hours. Here's what we did: We reviewed their options with local internet service providers, negotiated a plan that hit the performance benchmarks they needed — and kept it well within budget. We secured a business-grade, high-speed connection with a failover backup for redundancy. The monthly cost came in lower than what they'd assumed a "real internet upgrade" would require. Then we helped them decommission the old server... properly wiping and disposing of the hardware, migrating the relevant data, and making sure nothing critical was left stranded on-premise. The result? They launched their new cloud PMS with full confidence. And, had a failover connection in place for the moments when the internet (or the cloud) has other plans. Cloud-based practice management software requires a reliable foundation to perform as advertised. Most dental software companies - including the four featured here - design their cloud platforms with the assumption that your network can handle real-time cloud traffic. And that's a fair assumption... if your infrastructure is actually ready for it. Here's what that means in practice: A reliable, high-speed internet connection preferably with a failover or backup connection at each location

Secure, properly configured network infrastructure: especially important for handling of patient data (HIPAA-compliant)

Managed endpoint devices: workstations, tablets, and imaging hardware that stay updated and protected

A clear plan for your existing server (if you’re making the switch from server to cloud): whether that’s decommissioning, repurposing, or replacing it This is the gap we see most often when practices make the leap to cloud-based systems: the PMS decision gets careful attention, and the IT infrastructure gets an afterthought. They're two sides of the same coin. Ready to Make the Move to a Cloud-Based Practice Management Software? Here's a Simple Plan to Get Started If you're seriously evaluating a cloud-based PMS upgrade, here's a straightforward path forward: Narrow to two or three options based on your practice size, growth goals, and the factors most important to your team. Request live demos... not recorded ones. Walk through real workflows: scheduling an appointment, submitting a claim, running a production report. Talk to current users and ask the vendor for references from practices similar to yours. What was onboarding really like? How's support six months in? Assess your IT infrastructure before you commit to get a clear picture of your network reliability, security posture, and hardware readiness. Review the full contract to understand the total cost of ownership, data portability rights, and what's included vs. what costs extra. And if you have questions about dental software management requirements for your specific setup, or want to make sure your infrastructure is ready before you commit to a platform... we're here to help! A people-first culture drives the service excellence that sets Curve apart ALPHARETTA, Ga., April 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Curve Dental®, a leading provider of cloud-based practice management software for dental professionals, today announced it has been named a 2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces award winner. The award is based entirely on employee feedback gathered through a confidential survey administered by Energage, the HR research and technology company behind the Top Workplaces program for the last two decades. Continue Reading

Curve Dental recognized as a 2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces winner, highlighting the dental software company's team-driven culture shaping its award-winning service and support. In a competitive dental software market, Curve Dental has built its name on something that can't be replicated by software alone: best-in-class customer service. And it starts from within. When employees feel supported, valued, and genuinely invested in their work, that energy translates directly into the experience dental practices receive every day — from the technology they rely on to the people who stand behind it. When asked to describe Curve Dental's culture in their own words, employees used terms like "friendly", "inclusive", "supportive", and "team-oriented". Survey results highlighted particular strengths in manager effectiveness — with employees reporting that their managers actively support their growth, respect their time, and genuinely care about their concerns. "In the dental software space, our customer service and product set us apart — and that doesn't happen by accident," said Jana Macon, President of Curve Dental. "It happens because we have a team that genuinely wants to be here and shares a unified vision to serve our customers with purpose and passion. We've always believed that when you invest in your people, it shows up everywhere — in the product, in the support we offer our customers, and in the relationships we build across the dental community." Curve Dental's core values — collaborative, focused, trustworthy, gracious, and innovative — shape how teams work together and how the company shows up for the dental practices it continues to serve. The company strives to foster an environment where every employee feels heard, supported, and connected to work that matters. "Every decision our practices make is about their patients. Every decision we make is about our practices. That's why being named a 2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces winner matters — not only as a milestone for us, but as validation of how we show up for our dental practices," adds Macon. "This recognition is proof that a purpose-driven team creates happy customers, and that's the foundation everything else is built on." To learn more about working at Curve Dental and explore open opportunities, visit https://www.curvedental.com/careers. About Curve Dental: Curve Dental provides the leading all-in-one cloud-based practice management software for dental professionals and practices across the United States and Canada. From the start, the company has been singularly focused on the dental industry and is committed to delivering the best all-in-one dental practice management and patient engagement software for practices of all sizes. Curve Dental is privately held, with operations in Provo, Utah; Alpharetta, Georgia; Calgary, Alberta; and Aberdeen, Scotland. 38% of DSO revenue flows directly through the phone — new patient acquisition, case acceptance, hygiene utilization, reactivation. Every dollar of growth you're planning begins with a conversation. That means scaling from three locations to five doesn't just multiply your capacity. It multiplies every communication gap that already exists across your current offices. The practices that expand without fixing their phone infrastructure first don't just struggle — they lose revenue in ways that never show up in a production report.

The Numbers That Define What Expansion Actually Costs You

Before your fourth or fifth location opens its doors, consider what is happening right now across your existing three:

25–40% of new patient calls to dental offices do not result in a booked appointment — even when someone picks up the phone. (Peerlogic)
